analysis.investment_thesis: Admach is a tiny (INR 130 Cr) special-purpose machinery maker with a 0.44% ROE — earnings are effectively nil, so the 14.9x P/E is misleading and PEG is incalculable. No visible growth story, no moat, and no margin of safety — this is not a Lynch buy.
key_strengths: Niche in custom SPM/automation — a space with India capex tailwinds if execution improves
Promoter holding at 52.95% shows skin in the game
Small base (INR 130 Cr mcap) leaves theoretical room to scale if orders flow
key_risks: ROE of 0.44% is effectively zero — capital is not earning
No disclosed earnings growth rate, so PEG cannot be justified at 14.9x P/E
Micro-cap industrial with negligible FII/DII interest (~2%) — liquidity and governance risk
red_flags: ROE <1% despite a positive P/E suggests razor-thin earnings on a tiny base
Project-based SPM revenue is lumpy and customer-concentrated
Recently listed BSE SME-profile name with thin institutional validation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Lynch lens, the story is missing. Special-purpose machines are a decent niche riding India's manufacturing/automation capex, but a 0.44% ROE tells me the business is not yet earning its cost of capital — a P/E of 14.9x on near-zero earnings means the denominator is tiny, not that the stock is cheap. Without disclosed revenue/EPS growth, I cannot compute a PEG, and Lynch doesn't buy blind hope at 14x earnings on a INR 130 Cr industrial with no visible operating leverage yet.

I'd want to see two consecutive years of 20%+ revenue growth, ROE climbing toward mid-teens, and an order book that proves the SPM pipeline is real before touching this. Until then it's a classic "too small, too unproven" — pass, revisit after 2-4 quarters of evidence.
